title: EdgeFlow prefetch governor and latency sentinel
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see sporadic p99 bursts on mixed small/medium sequence workloads when admission spikes coincide with heterogeneous kernel paths (FP16 vs int8 kernels). Current admission logic uses a single threshold heuristic which cannot adapt to runtime kernel fit or attention-slot fragmentation. This ticket introduces EdgeFlow: a prefetch governor that combines short-horizon token-window predictions, an attention-slot aware batch shaper, and a lightweight kernel prober. The goal is to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput and not regressing average token cost.

Scope:
- Admission/controller: implement a reservoir-based short-window governor that reserves slots for latency-sensitive requests and throttles opportunistic prefill to maintain p99 SLO.
- Batch shaping: group requests into attention-slot compatible lanes (e.g., similar prefix lengths and attention memory footprint) to improve kernel packing density.
- Kernel probing: on new model variants or quantization paths, run cheap micro-probes to estimate kernel latency under current load and pick the kernel path at admission time.
- Latency sentinel: end-to-end p95/p99 sentinel that tags requests with admission metadata and correlates kernel selection, attention-lane, and queueing time to identify root causes.

Non-goals: full RL-based admission tuning (prototype only), cross-region routing changes, and UI work (console integration is separate ticket).

Rationale: By moving kernel selection earlier in the request lifecycle and shaping batches into lanes with compatible attention/resource characteristics, we can reduce kernel warmup and fragmentation which contributes to tail spikes. Coupling this with a lightweight sentinel for observability will make regressions actionable and enable fast rollbacks or policy tuning.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency on mixed small+medium internal benchmark reduced by >=30% compared to baseline (measured over 24h cluster test)
end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) does not decrease by more than 5% for steady workloads
no increase in average per-token cost (cloud billing estimate) > 2%
kernel probe runs in <=1ms added admission latency for cold probes and <=0.1ms when cached
sentinel traces can attribute 95% of p99 events to a combination of admission decision, kernel path, or attention-lane mismatch
feature gated behind runtime flag and gradual rollout (canary) supported in runtime-1.24
implementation_steps: Design governor proto: window size, reservoir policy, and fairness rules (2 days)
Add attention-slot classifier at request ingress that emits lane tags (3 days)
Implement kernel prober: micro-bench endpoint + cache with eviction policy (4 days)
Admission integration: combine reservoir, lane occupancy, and kernel-fit score to accept/defer/redirect requests (5 days)
Latency sentinel instrumentation: add tags (admission_time, lane, kernel_choice) and custom metrics for p50/p95/p99 (2 days)
Run cluster experiments: canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with performance dashboards and kill-switch (3 days)
Write rollout playbook and support automation for runtime flag toggles (1 day)
PRs, code review, and perf regression signoff (continuous)
Console/Docs follow-up ticket for user-visible metrics (separate PM ticket)
notes_and_tradeoffs: We accept slight additional complexity at admission in exchange for significantly lower tail. The kernel prober introduces tiny extra CPU but avoids many slow kernel selections downstream.
Prefetching more aggressively reduces cold-kernel penalties but increases cache pressure; governor will be conservative by default and tuned from experiments.
Attention-lane grouping may temporarily increase waiting time for some single-request flows; reservoir ensures a small fast-path quota for latency-critical tokens.
We will not attempt cross-model kernel synthesis here; the probe is strictly per-model-variant and hardware profile.
Feature will be behind a runtime flag and have a hard kill-switch at the routing layer to disable if unforeseen regressions occur.
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Spiked initial design doc. Prototype of attention-slot classifier looks promising on local traces — lane collision reduced from 37% -> 12% on sample workload.
2026-03-04 Dev Review (Ravi Kapoor): Suggest keeping probe result TTL short (30s) in multi-tenant env to avoid stale kernel-fit under load variance.
2026-03-06 Performance (Ava Patel): Micro-probe implemented; cold probe ~0.9ms, cached probe ~0.08ms. Adding probe to admission path increases median admission by 0.05ms when cached.
2026-03-08 Experiment Run 1 (canary 5%): p99 reduced from 420ms -> 290ms on our synthetic burst test; throughput unchanged. Observed two outlier patterns related to attention-slot misclassification.
2026-03-10 Design Decision: Add quick reclassification on prefill boundary to reduce misclassification. Also increased reservoir fast-path from 3% -> 5% for tail-sensitive tenants.
2026-03-11 QA (Emilia Ross): End-to-end sentinel traces are working. Able to filter p99 events and attribute to "kernel_choice" in 82% of cases; need to reach 95% — will add queue-time tagging.
2026-03-13 Rollout Note (Ava Patel): Canary 20% stable for 6h. Measured p99 down 35% on mixed traffic; cost delta +0.6%. Next step: 50% canary tomorrow morning with extended soak.
2026-03-14 PM Feedback (Diego Ramos): Ensure runbook includes steps to revert lane grouping (config toggle) and to automatically disable kernel probing if probe errors >1% over 1h.
